subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: What should OpenClaw do by default when an agent turn emits assistant text that looks like a tool call but no structured toolCall/toolUse content exists?
rationale: The current code intentionally combines warning-only diagnostics, bounded compatibility promotion, and scoped Gateway HTTP enforcement; choosing stricter rejection, forced retry, or broader promotion changes both security posture and local-model compatibility.

options.title: Define bounded enforcement
options.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and implement it across the agent loop, provider wrappers, Gateway docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep warning-only compatibility
options.body: Document fake tool-call text as provider/model incompatibility and accept that it can still reach transcripts or visible replies without a real tool call.

options.title: Split broader claim checks
options.body: Limit this issue to syntactic fake tool-call text and keep natural-language success-claim verification under separate response-gate or ledger tracking.

recommendation.title: Define bounded enforcement
recommendation.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and implement it across the agent loop, provider wrappers, Gateway docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a core agent-runtime security/default policy, and steipete has the strongest recent history on the relevant agent boundary.
